editorial:
Invasion of the Bee Girls is a 1973 US science-fiction horror film directed by Denis Sanders from a script by Nicholas Meyer. Wikipedia lists Sequoia Pictures as the production company and Centaur Releasing as distributor. It was released in 1973 and also circulated as 'Graveyard Tramps'. A reuser might want it for its place in Meyer's early career.

The rights trap is that the film's public-domain status is not established. A work published in 1973 is protected for 95 years from publication. Renewal was automatic, so a missing renewal cannot put it in the public domain. The only realistic route is publication without a valid copyright notice. A user review on an Internet Archive upload says the film carries a valid 1973 notice. That review is unverified. Archive.org's 'Public Domain Mark' labels are uploader-applied and are not evidence. Do not treat any Internet Archive copy as cleared. Check the notice on the film itself (title card or end card) first. A registration search can add context but does not settle the question.
faq: Is Invasion of the Bee Girls in the public domain?

Not established. A 1973 film's renewal was automatic, so it is protected for 95 years unless it was published without a proper copyright notice. A reviewer on an Internet Archive upload reports a valid 1973 notice. Treat it as protected.
Can I use the Internet Archive copies?

Do not rely on them. The 'Public Domain Mark' on those items is set by the uploader and is not a rights determination. Copies may also come from home-video sources such as DVD, and release extras or new material on those could carry separate protection.
